M020.by: Sample for the design review, Claude Opus (agent)
M020.summary: PETG is unfilled glycol-modified polyethylene terephthalate, the copolyester its makers sell for functional parts that meet water, sun and handling: brackets, holders, outdoor fixtures. It prints in an open machine, and most of its products need no heated chamber. Makers stress low warping and good bonding between layers, and warn that it holds hard to the bed. Under load it deflects at {hdt045.median} ({hdt045.label}). Notched impact is thinly published, with {charpyNotched.n} products giving a comparable Charpy value.

M001.by: Sample for the design review, Claude Opus (agent)
M001.summary: PLA is unfilled polylactic acid, which makers sell for prototypes, visual models, jigs and classroom printing. It prints without a heated chamber on a cool bed, and its makers describe little warping. It prints amorphous and softens near its glass transition, so under load it deflects at {hdt045.median} ({hdt045.label}). Some of its products are toughened or filled versions; their values are set apart from the plain products'. Few products publish a notched impact value on a comparable basis.

M110.by: Sample for the design review, Claude Opus (agent)
M110.summary: PCTG-GF is PCTG copolyester filled with glass fibre, sold by {makers} makers for tooling, fixtures and manufacturing aids. Its makers describe it as easy to print in an open machine, with low shrinkage, and their sheets give a drying schedule. Some of its products need a hardened nozzle. Under load it deflects at {hdt045.median} ({hdt045.label}). Little else is compared: no product states the orientation of its tensile bars, and its only price in the sample comes from a foreign listing.
